title: Feedback polygon: annotated customer requests (July 2025)
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, annotated synthesis of customer-facing signals collected between May–July 2025 focused on: hosted API pain points, deterministic latency expectations, model fallback behavior, and small product changes customers repeatedly ask for. The goal is to create an actionable micro-roadmap of low-effort/high-impact fixes and a short list of candidate experiments for product and engineering to evaluate.

Context and scope
- Source mix: support threads, CSM notes from enterprise pilots, evaluation lab transcripts, and two NPS follow-up interviews (mid-market).
- Not exhaustive; intentionally narrow: we prioritized requests that appeared 5+ times across independent customers or created clear operational risk (SLA/regulatory).
- Tone: exploratory — includes candidate technical constraints and quick feasibility flags for engineering.

Executive snapshot (TL;DR)
1) High-frequency asks: clearer per-request latency SLOs, more transparent routing fallback logs, and easier ways to pin a model variant for a route.
2) Low-effort wins: expose per-request region tag in response headers; add a small console toggle to surface active fallback events; create a simple API param to prefer cost-optimized variants when throughput > X TPS. Estimated 1–3 sprint effort for each.
3) Medium effort experiments: canary-level rollout controls by percent of tokens (not just requests); affinity routing heuristics (session stickiness + hot-kv-cache awareness). 3–8 sprints.

Key themes (annotated)
1) Latency predictability (top signal)
- Pattern: customers building chat UIs complain when 99th percentile spikes unpredictably (bursts during concurrent background jobs, or cross-model fallback).
- Representative quote: "We calibrate UX timeouts to 500ms and if it goes to 900ms users get dropped — there’s no readout we can programmatically rely on."
- Severity: high for real-time UIs.
- Candidate responses: publish per-model 95/99 latency profiles by request size on Console; allow route-level latency SLO tags and automated fallback suppression when SLO is critical.
- Feasibility note: publishing historical distributions is low friction; suppressing fallback for SLO-critical routes requires coordination with routing stack (compatibility check).

2) Observability of routing & fallback decisions
- Pattern: incidents where customers see degraded quality after fallback to cheaper variants and want exact reason/context.
- Representative quote: "We saw an odd hallucination burst and can’t tell if it was a model downgrade or a quantization switch."
- Severity: medium-high (trust/diagnostic overhead).
- Candidate responses: add event log entries (route,fallback-reason,variant-id,timestamp) surfaced in Console and optionally forwarded to customer webhook. Small API change: include variant_id and fallback_reason in response meta.
- Feasibility: variant_id in response header — trivial. Centralized event stream per-customer — moderate.

3) Pinning and rollout ergonomics
- Pattern: product teams want to pin a route to a specific model/quantization variant while gradually testing new variants. Current rollout controls are coarse.
- Representative quote: "We don’t want automatic fallbacks to defeat a canary — need a quarantined canary with manual approval."
- Severity: medium.
- Candidate responses: add a 'pinned' flag on routes + a canary throttle by token percentage (see experiments).
- Feasibility: requires small Console + routing-policy change; can reuse existing rollout A/B infra with another metric.

4) Cost/transparency levers for heavy-embedding workloads
- Pattern: embedding-heavy customers want per-route memory hints and better batching knobs to lower cost; confusion around billing granularity for batched embeddings.
- Representative quote: "We batch at client-side and see billing surprises when Redwood auto-batches with other tenants — we want predictable unit accounting."
- Severity: medium.
- Candidate responses: expose a 'batching_hint' config for routes and a 'dedicated-bill-window' option for heavy embedding jobs.

Representative customer vignettes (anonymized)
- Fintech analytics mid-market (Pilot): requests explicit 99th-percentile guarantees and a console view showing time-of-day variance + active fallback events. High priority to their CS team; legal asked about SLA language.
- Messaging startup (PLG): needs a simple toggle to disable automatic model downgrades per-app basis during product experiments. Will accept slightly higher cost in exchange for quality stability.
- Enterprise healthcare customer: wants audit trails for model variant selection and cryptographic proof of model pinning for compliance.

Micro-feature proposals (ranked, quick wins first)
1) Response headers: region, variant_id, fallback_reason (string) — SDK + REST. (Est effort: 1 sprint)
2) Console: small 'Fallback events' card per route with last 48h sampled events + quick link to raw logs. (Est effort: 1 sprint)
3) Route config: 'prefer_cost_variant_when_throughput_gt' numeric param — routing will attempt cheaper compatible variants only when route TPS exceeds threshold. (Est effort: 2 sprints)
4) Pin by token-perc canary: allow setting canary_percent as token-level allocation (not request-level). (Est effort: 3–5 sprints)
5) Batching hint + invoice window for heavy embeddings: (Est effort: 3 sprints)

Engineering feasibility flags (quick)
- Adding headers (variant_id/region) is trivial; ensure header format stable across SDKs.
- Fallback event stream requires privacy review (what we log) and sizing estimate for high-volume customers; consider sampling and opt-in webhooks.
- Token-percentage canary needs token accounting at routing time; we have existing token accounting telemetry inside serving-runtime but will need to surface decisions to the orchestrator.

Suggested near-term roadmap (30/60/90)
- 30 days: Ship headers + basic console tile for fallback events (MVP). Start privacy review for event content. Open RFC on canary-by-token design.
- 60 days: Implement route-level 'prefer_cost_variant_when_throughput_gt' and set up an internal beta with two PLG customers.
- 90 days: Prototype token-percent canary and batch-hint routing; run experiments with Dedicated customers who can commit to pilot.

Metrics & success criteria
- Reduction in customer support threads referencing unexplained latency spikes (target: -40% within 60 days post-MVP).
- Adoption: Number of routes using 'pin' or 'prefer_cost_variant' config (target: 10 early customers in first quarter).
- Observability: volume of fallback event exports — use as signal for further investments.

Open questions / discussion points
- Privacy & logging: what fallback metadata is safe to include in outbound webhooks or logs? (legal/infosec input required)
- Billing semantics: can we surface batched-embedding billing breakdowns without major invoice changes? (finance input)
- UX friction: how to show 'variant_id' meaningfully to non-technical PMs? Suggest a human-friendly alias mapping in Console.

Next steps (owner + timeframe)
- PRD draft for headers + console tile: Priya N. (CS) + Matt R. (observability) — draft by 2025-07-28.
- Technical RFC for token-percent canary: Lina C. (product infra) + Diego M. (serving-runtime) — RFC by 2025-08-05.
- Legal/Finance check-in on logging & billing: Sofia A. (CS) to coordinate — meeting target 2025-07-24.

Appendix: quick links to sample threads
- Support case 11234: transcript showing fallback -> hallucination (anonymized).
- Slack thread: #cs-pilot-fintech (see linked_artifacts).
- Internal eval notes: embed-batch-sensitivity-2025-06 (Confluence).

Notes to self
- Keep this doc lightweight; anticipate follow-up with specific beta customers for each micro-feature.
- Avoid bundling everything into a single large project — aim for incremental wins that materially reduce noise for customers.

End of file
